svg.title: How wins above replacement works
svg.desc: Wins above replacement (WAR). How much a pilot adds to whatever side it flies for, in matches like the live page's. Borrowed from baseball. The replacement is the script, the hand-written pilot. A vertical sequence starts with 1. Many matches, pilots drawn at random. The key names pilots A, B, C and D, and S = the script. Three example matches each show three azure strike craft on the left facing right and three ember strike craft on the right facing left, seen from above. Each craft has its pilot's letter beneath it. In match 1, azure has A, S, C and ember has B, D, S. Azure won. In match 2, azure has S, B, D and ember has A, S, C. Ember won. In match 3, azure has D, A, S and ember has S, C, B. The result is draw, half each. There are ... and thousands more. Each strike craft's pilot is drawn at random, ship by ship, from the pilots being rated and the script. Missions, line-ups and commanders are drawn as on the live page. An arrow leads to 2. A fit sorts out who added what. Because the draws are random, each pilot flies beside and against every other. A statistical fit over all the matches at once tells each pilot's share of a win from its teammates'. It allows for the mission, the side and the commanders. Below the text, three small boxes labelled azure won, ember won and draw, half each feed through thin converging lines into a small box labelled the fit. Another arrow leads to 3. Each pilot's score. A horizontal dot-and-whisker chart has a vertical line labelled 0: the script's level. A is clearly to the right of zero, B a bit less, C small but right of zero, and D's line crosses zero. Its axis note is wins added per 100 matches, over the script flying the same ships. The key says dot: the estimate, and line: the margin of error, the range the true value very likely lies in. For every match a pilot flew in: the fit's chance that its side wins, minus the same with the script flying its ships. Averaged and times 100. A draw counts half. The final box says Read it within one table. Compare pilots within one WAR table, not across nights. Each table is its own fit, over its own matches and its own pilots. A pilot's score moves with the company it is rated in.
